editorial.description_en: A mud wall in shade — brown by any reading, and much quieter than the fired colours beside it.
editorial.description_ja: 日かげの泥壁のような、おだやかな茶。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.516, C 0.054, h 70.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 泥 (doro, mud) + 壁 (kabe, wall). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Mud Wall" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 泥壁. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — chiri-ba at ΔE00 7.4, furu-kawa at ΔE00 7.9, kare-eda at ΔE00 9.4. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (250°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
